key_insight: Fourier-circuit configuration changes hybrid PointNet–quantum classification performance and noise sensitivity, with IQFT-After leading on ideal KITTI simulations but degrading more under noise.
engineering_relevance: Hardware-aware circuit selection matters: removing final QFT SWAP gates reduces complexity while preserving Pauli-Z features up to a fixed permutation absorbable by the classification head.
method: Combine classical PointNet feature extraction, amplitude encoding, and a variational quantum circuit.
Compare No-QFT, Full-QFT-After, QFT-no-swap, IQFT-After, and Trainable-QFT.
Evaluate classification, circuit complexity, and robustness under IBM FakeManilaV2 simulated noise.
evidence_signal: Across KITTI, nuScenes, and PandaSet with three random seeds, ideal KITTI weighted F1 reached 0.857 ± 0.033 for IQFT-After versus 0.838 ± 0.023 for No-QFT.
watch_item: Simulation results do not establish quantum advantage or real-device performance; noise changes circuit rankings, and minority-class outcomes vary by dataset.
paper_title: QFT-Based Hybrid PointNet-Quantum Neural Networks for LiDAR Point-Cloud Classification
